validation.notes: Root cause: packages/agent/src/harness/runtime/drive/tools.ts, recoverToolInvocation chose the replay branch on `call.replay === "safe" && tool?.replay === "safe"` and ignored its `cancelled` argument. In the parallel drive path that argument is the durable control status sampled per call (runParallel), so a batch that becomes cancel_requested while earlier calls are being dispatched still cleared the replay checkpoint (pending tool output deleted), re-invoked the tool with replay: 'safe', and published the replayed effect result instead of interruption evidence. Fix: guard the replay branch with `!cancelled` (one-line change, no other production edits), so a cancelled effect_pending call falls through to readCheckpoint + interruptedOutcome: no checkpoint clearing, no tool invocation, interrupted evidence carrying the durable snapshot/details published once and settled. Non-cancelled safe/safe calls still clear the checkpoint, invoke exactly once, and settle the result. Regression (.prale-eval/regression.mjs) drives the real recoverToolInvocation through .prale-eval/subject.mjs with observable boundary fakes and asserts: cancelled safe/safe -> no 'clear'/'invoke'/'effect-complete' events, a 'read' before a final 'publish', isError interrupted message containing the durable-progress snapshot plus interruption marker and checkpoint details, no effect result leaked; same for cancelled safe/never, cancelled safe/missing-tool, and a cancelled safe/safe run whose effect probe would throw if invoked; non-cancelled safe/safe -> exact event sequence ['clear','invoke','effect-complete','publish'] with the successful effect result; non-cancelled never/safe -> interrupted evidence. Verified the script exits 1 with an AssertionError ('cancellation must not clear the replay checkpoint') against the pre-fix source and exits 0 after the fix via the exact validation command from the workspace root. Limitation: repository dependency-based checks (vitest/tsc) were not run because node_modules is absent and installing dependencies is out of scope; only Node 24's built-in TypeScript stripping and VM modules were used.
